title: Per-word runtime fingerprinting and cache-penalty reconciler
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Add lightweight per-word (per-token) runtime fingerprints that correlate micro-timings with prefix/KV-cache events and upstream kernel handoffs. Produce an aggregated, privacy-safe 'cache-penalty' metric per request that can be joined to billing reconciliations and latency dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation emits an OpenTelemetry span per emission slice with attributes: token_index, token_length, micro_ms, cache_hit:boolean, cache_latency_ms, kernel_id.
End-to-end pipeline ingests token spans into the telemetry stream and materializes an aggregated cache-penalty score per request in metrics-store within 60s.
Queryable view in Console: request-level token latency waterfall with cache-hit overlay and cost attribution column.
Sampling controls exist (1%, 10%, 100%) and per-customer opt-out respects privacy flags.
Observed overhead on p99 latency increase < 0.5% in canary rollout at 10% traffic.
Security review completed and KMS/E2EE considerations documented for telemetry payloads.
notes: Motivation: current billing/latency dashboards operate at request or token-bucket granularity; customers need visibility into where cache misses drive token cost and p99 latency regressions.
We will call this metric set 'runtime_fingerprint' and derived 'cache_penalty_score' to avoid confusion with existing 'token-emission' traces.
Initial spike showed ~200ns additional overhead per token when running N=1 tracing; we'll rely on sampling and on-worker aggregation to reduce cardinality.
We must strip PII from any prompt snippets before including them in spans; default behavior is not to include prompt content.
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Chose OpenTelemetry protobuf spans (OTLP/gRPC) for portability across dedicated/private deployments.
2026-02-18: Agreed to attach only token_index and token_hash (not raw text) to spans; token_hash is truncated SHA256 (first 8 chars) for grouping.
2026-02-25: Use on-GPU pre-aggregation to emit per-request summaries to the telemetry agent to limit ingestion costs.
2026-03-03: Sampling tiers will be configurable by customer and by route; default 5% in hosted API.
implementation_steps: Add tracing hook in emission loop (runtime) to create 'token_emission' span with attributes listed in design doc.
Implement on-worker aggregator that rolls token spans into request_summary proto every X ms or on request completion.
Extend telemetry agent (collector) to accept request_summary and write to metrics-store and raw-trace S3 for 7-day retention.
Create transformer job that computes 'cache_penalty_score' and stores per-request record in metrics-store for dashboards and billing joins.
Add Console widgets and Alert rules: per-route cache_penalty p95 > baseline triggers investigation runbook link.
Run canary on internal team with 1% traffic, measure overhead, iterate, then ramp to 10% and 25% before full rollout.
risks: Telemetry cardinality blowup if we emit per-token raw spans for 100% traffic; mitigated by sampling and pre-aggregation.
Latency/CPU overhead on hot GPU workers if hooks do heavy processing; mitigated by minimal attribute collection and deferring work to aggregator thread.
Regulatory/PII risk if prompt snippets are accidentally included; security review required and tests to verify stripping.
Billing reconciliation complexity: cache_penalty_score must be validated against existing per-token cost model to avoid double-counting.
testing_plan: Unit tests for span attribute generation and token_hash correctness.
Load test with simulated multi-tenant traffic to measure ingestion rates and aggregator CPU usage.
Canary on staging with full sampling enabled for a short window to compare computed cache_penalty_score vs baseline instrumentation (existing billing probe).
Security tests that verify no prompt content persists in telemetry payloads and KMS keys are used for any stored artifacts requiring encryption.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag behind 'token_fingerprint' off by default in hosted and private.
Phase 1: Internal canary (10% internal traffic) for 72h. Validate overhead and accuracy.
Phase 2: Opt-in customers by support toggle; monitor metrics for ingestion and SLO regression for 2 weeks.
Phase 3: Gradual default enablement to 25% then 100% with sampling defaults. Publish release notes and dashboard links.
monitoring_post_release: SLOs: p99 request latency deviation vs baseline, ingestion error rate, collector CPU usage.
Dashboards: 'Token Fingerprint Overview', 'Cache Penalty by Route', 'Top requests by cache_penalty_score'.
Alerts: telemetry ingestion failure > 1% over 5m; cache_penalty_score spike > 3x baseline for a route.
